transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-04
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording: Yes (auto)

Summary: quick sync to align go-live readiness for the Moonstone pilot on Redwood Inference. Covered VPC setup, SSO, performance targets, rollback/fallback plans, and next steps for a short production pilot. Some audio dropouts in the middle; a couple of names got mis-transcribed.

Topics:
- Production network & VPC peering
- SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning
- Performance SLOs (p99 latency, throughput)
- Data retention / audit logs / encryption (KMS)
- Pilot timeline and success criteria

Action items (spoken during call): see action_items metadata above.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We're gonna be pretty focused today, just a readiness check for the pilot, quick sync on blockers. Diego's gonna cover onboarding playbook and Priya will do the infra deep bits.
[00:18] Oliver Grant: Great, thanks Maya. We got the core team here. Rashmi, Tariq and Elena on our side. We're expecting to start pilot traffic next Monday, so want to validate network and SSO steps.
[00:28] Diego Ramos: Awesome. I'll run through the onboarding checklist, timing, and what we need from Moonstone; then Priya will jump into VPC/VPN and the dedicated vs hosted decision points.
[00:36] Rashmi Patel: One quick thing — our infra team prefers private deployment in VPC with customer-managed keys. We might have to do an on-prem box for certain workloads, just flagging that early.
[00:48] Priya Kapoor: Totally understood. We support Private deployments and customer KMS/HSM integrations. For the initial pilot we usually do a VPC peering and a small Redwood Dedicated pool behind a CIDR-restricted ELB.
[01:02] Tariq Noor: When you say "Redwood Dedicated pool" do you mean reserved GPUs in your cloud, or are we talking about bringing your runtime on prem? We have some pieces that need to stay on premise for PCI scope.
[01:15] Priya Kapoor: Good question. For the pilot we can do two paths: 1) Redwood Dedicated in your VPC (we provision reserved nodes in the same cloud region and VPC peering), or 2) an on-prem bundle which is more involved. Given your PCI concerns, path 1 keeps data in your VPC and keys in your KMS; path 2 is for fully air-gapped.
[01:36] Elena Park: The timeline matters — the on-prem approach is gonna add weeks. We were hoping for a fast start. Is the VPC approach HIPAA/PCI friendly if we manage keys?
[01:47] Diego Ramos: Yes, we have customers doing PCI scoped workloads with VPC + customer-managed KMS and strict audit logs. We'll send our SOC 2 + supplemental PCI notes.
[01:56] Oliver Grant: Okay, send docs. Also, how do you handle auditing and session traces? We need full request logs for a minimum of 90 days.
[02:07] Priya Kapoor: We can export audit logs to your Cloud Storage or SIEM via a secure forwarder. There's a retention config; default is 30 days but we can extend to 90 as an add-on. I'll include the log retention config in the checklist.
[02:22] Tariq Noor: Another perf question — we saw in your benchmarks that p99 varies with sequence length. Our live prompts will average 800 tokens on the first pass, but we do a lot of short follow-ups. Can you help size the pool so latency stays under 250ms p95?
[02:37] Priya Kapoor: Right, sequence length distribution matters a lot. For an 800-token average you should expect higher tail latency. For p95 <250ms using a 7B-ish family model is unlikely at that length; if you can shard the prompt or precompute embeddings for some parts, that helps. Alternatively we can use a larger model variant with quantized kernels and a tuned batching policy.
[02:57] Oliver Grant: Hmm ok. Our product team will consider reducing prompt length; can Redwood help with batching/caching suggestions?
[03:05] Priya Kapoor: Absolutely — Redwood Optimize can recommend batching and KV cache settings. We'll run a workload profile after you provide sample prompts.
[03:13] Elena Park: We'll share sample prompts by Friday.
[03:18] Maya Chen: Perfect. A few non-technical things — SSO, SCIM, and RBAC. Tariq, who's our identity owner?
[03:25] Tariq Noor: That's me. We use Okta and SCIM provisioning is required. We also want SAML based SSO with enforced MFA.
[03:33] Diego Ramos: We support Okta SAML and SCIM. We'll share the SAML metadata and SCIM endpoint; integration usually takes a couple days. We'll also provide a test account matrix for you to validate roles.
[03:45] Rashmi Patel: Regarding egress — we need egress to be locked down to our tooling. If the dedicated nodes are in our VPC, is there any outbound call to Redwood control plane?
[03:55] Priya Kapoor: For Private deployments there is optional control plane connectivity. For fully air-gapped you can run with a local control plane; for VPC peering we have a secure control plane tunnel that uses a specific set of egress IPs. We'll provide the allowlist.
[04:10] Oliver Grant: Good. Please send the allowlist. Also our security team wants to see KMS key rotation policies.
[04:17] Priya Kapoor: We'll include KMS integration docs and rotation guidance. We support CMEK and HSM integrations in Private.
[04:25] Maya Chen: Quick question on fallbacks — if Dedicated nodes spike or a rollout goes bad, what's the fallback behavior?
[04:33] Priya Kapoor: We have built-in fallback policies: route to a lower-cost hosted variant in another region or a smaller model family. You can configure automatic fallback or manual. For the pilot we recommend manual fallback so your team observes behavior first.
[04:48] Elena Park: Is there an option to replay requests to a canary model offline to check quality drift?
[04:53] Diego Ramos: Yes, we have replay and shadowing tooling; we can set up a replay pipeline to run in a staging environment so you can validate outputs before a cutover.
[05:02] Tariq Noor: Billing question — during the pilot how are tokens counted if we do retries? We want transparent cost modeling.
[05:09] Diego Ramos: Tokens are counted per request and per generation. Retries you initiate will be billed. We can provide an estimated cost sheet based on prompt profiles. Also we can set usage quotas to prevent runaway spend.
[05:20] Rashmi Patel: We need token billing mapped to our internal cost centers. Is a per-route granularity possible?
[05:26] Diego Ramos: Yep, we have per-route accounting and tag-based attribution so you can tie usage to teams.
[05:32] Oliver Grant: Ok, next — runbook for incident response. Who's the on-call at Redwood if there's a latency outage?
[05:39] Maya Chen: Diego and our CSM team handle pager escalation during pilots; we also have an enterprise on-call rota for Dedicated customers. We'll share the on-call matrix and SLO targets.
[05:48] Elena Park: Can we get 15-minute on-call SLA during the pilot window?
[05:52] Diego Ramos: For pilots we aim for 30-minute pager response; enterprise SLA of 15 minutes is available as an add-on. We can discuss upgrading if you need it.
[06:02] Tariq Noor: A couple of nitty-gritty networking things — do you support VPC peering and Transit Gateway architectures? Also how do you handle cross-AZ latency?
[06:12] Priya Kapoor: We support both peering and Transit Gateway. For cross-AZ latency we recommend placing nodes in the same AZ as your downstream services; our runtime supports rack-local servlets and cross-AZ affinity. Also we'll provide kernel-level affinities for lower tail latency.
[06:29] Oliver Grant: Any gotchas around our firewall rules?
[06:32] Priya Kapoor: Allowlist the control-plane IPs we send, open the mTLS port for the runtime, and allow egress to your SIEM endpoint for logs. We'll send a network diagram and a checklist.
[06:46] Elena Park: Workflow question — we want a runbook for rollout, rollback and communications. Can Redwood help author that with us?
[06:53] Diego Ramos: Yes, Diego and Maya can co-author the runbook with your SREs. We'll add a communication tree and playbooks for common incidents.
[07:02] Rashmi Patel: Also need a dry-run — can we do a 48-hour soak test with synthetic traffic and watch the metrics?
[07:07] Priya Kapoor: Absolutely. We recommend a two-phase: 24-hour functional test, then 48-hour soak. We'll run them in staging and capture perf traces.
[07:16] Maya Chen: Let's pause for a second — any outstanding blockers preventing pilot start?
[07:21] Oliver Grant: Network allowlist pending, SOC2 docs pending, and we need pricing confirmation. Not blockers but prerequisites.
[07:30] Diego Ramos: I'll send the pricing tiers and a pilot addendum today.
[07:34] Elena Park: On the security docs, can you combine SOC2 and the KMS notes into one package? It's easier for our review board.
[07:40] Priya Kapoor: Yes, we'll bundle SOC2 + KMS + SAML integration notes into a single PDF.
[07:46] Tariq Noor: One last thing — latency SLOs. Can we lock p95 <200ms for short prompts (<128 tokens) and pilot target p99 <1.2s for long prompts?
[07:57] Priya Kapoor: We can commit to p95 <200ms on short prompts for a dedicated pool sized appropriately. For long prompts p99 <1.2s is plausible with a larger instance profile and tuned batching, we'll include recommended pool size in the sizing doc.
[08:12] Oliver Grant: Great, that helps.
[08:15] Maya Chen: Okay, recap of next steps: Priya will send network diagram and deployment checklist; Diego will send pricing and pilot addendum; Maya will push SOC2 and SAML templates; Moonstone will send sample prompts and confirm allowlist. Anything to add?
[08:29] Elena Park: We'll aim to deliver sample prompts by Friday and confirm allowlist by Tuesday.
[08:34] Diego Ramos: I'll set up a follow-up slot for Friday afternoon to review prompts and initial sizing.
[08:39] Rashmi Patel: Quick note — audio dropped around 00:04:20, might be a missed sentence about canary configs, but I think we caught the gist.
[08:49] Maya Chen: Thanks. We'll record the missing canary details in the runbook and send the config template.
[08:56] Oliver Grant: Appreciate it — if we get these items in place, we can flip traffic next week.
[09:00] Maya Chen: Awesome. We'll follow up with the action items. Thanks everyone, meeting adjourned.
